subject: PulseAI hosted API: expected monthly burn + surge TPS — next steps
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Eli Walker <eli@pulseai.com>; Sophie Grant <sophie@pulseai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Follow-up: hosted API sizing + budget (recap & ask)

Thanks for taking the time today — great conversation. Recap below (please confirm or correct):

- Primary workload: conversational assistant + short summarization for support tickets (mix of 1–4 prompts per user session).
- Expected steady-state monthly token burn: ~80M–120M tokens (you quoted ~3–4M/day).
- Expected peak surge windows: up to ~110–140 TPS for short bursts (1–3 minutes) during product launches; baseline concurrency expected to be ~12–20 TPS.
- Desired unit target: $150 / 1M tokens (PulseAI wants to land a $$ number to model internal economics).
- Key constraints: data residency in us-east, ability to burst without rate-limiting user experience, and contract start in Sept.

Actions we proposed on the call:
1) Redwood to provide a priced band for hosted API (monthly slab pricing + burst cushions) that shows unit $/1M for committed tiers: 50M, 100M, 200M. Include a clear surge / peak TPS allowance and overage rates.
2) PulseAI to share last 30 days token export and an expected launch-day surge profile (timestamps). You mentioned attaching the export — thanks.
3) Align on SLOs for latency and a short canary run (1–2 weeks) post-commit.

Can you confirm the 80M–120M monthly range and the 110–140 TPS peak window? I attached a short template for the usage export you can drop into (pulseai_usage_csv.csv).

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Thanks, Hannah — solid notes. Confirming items and clarifications:

- Monthly: our current prod is ~35M tokens/month but with the planned launch we model a new product line at ~95M tokens/month in steady state (so your 80–120M range is correct).
- Peak: we observed spikes in our staging load tests simulating launch at ~125 TPS sustained for ~90s; we've budgeted for up to 150 TPS for safety.
- Unit target: the internal finance ask is to model $140–$160 / 1M tokens for P&L, so $150 / 1M is fine as a target to discuss.
- Residency: US-East1 (must be in a VPC-capable tenancy for the dedicated option later).
- Attachments: attaching the 30-day export and a synthetic surge trace.

Forwarding the export below for Redwood analysis. Let us know if you need per-endpoint breakdowns (we have conversational vs summarization).

—Eli

Nice recap. Quick internal notes and questions for pricing band construction: 

- We'll model three committed slabs and a surge buffer: 50M, 100M, 200M. For each slab we want to produce: committed $/1M, burst allowance (TPS-minute credits), and overage $/1M.
- From the export: please confirm the typical response length (tokens in/out). For initial modelling I assumed avg 18 tokens/request -> at 95M tokens/month that maps to ~5.3M requests/month (~180k/day). If you have a per-request token histogram please drop it in.
- For the surge profile: we price an included burst reservoir sized by TPS-minute units. For example, 125 TPS for 2 minutes = 15,000 TPS-minutes. We can express that as an included burst credit and then a per-1000-TPS-min overage.

Marissa: can you draft a pricing band table (CSV + short memo) that shows committed vs burst vs overage and two unit targets: $150/1M and $125/1M (PulseAI said $140–$160 so we bracket). Also include a short note on latency SLO assumptions per tier.

I'll prepare the technical sizing notes for the hosted runtime (KV cache, batching expectations) once they confirm the per-request token mix.

-Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Perfect — thanks for confirming, Eli. Next steps and timeline: 

1) PulseAI: drop the per-endpoint token histogram if possible (Eli). If not by EOD tomorrow, a quick sample of 500 requests will do.
2) Redwood (Marissa/Karthik): pricing bands + SOW draft (SOW_draft_v2.pdf stub) by Friday EOD. We'll show two unit bandings ($150 and $125 / 1M) and explicit surge credit math so you can pick which lane fits your finance model.
3) Schedule: propose a 30-minute follow-up next Tue (24 Aug) to walk through the pricing table and pick a slab. I've sent a calendar hold (tentative).

If PulseAI confirms they want a dedicated tenancy option later, we'll include a short appendix on Dedicated vs Hosted delta in the SOW.

Thanks again — looking forward to the pricing exercise.

Hannah
